title: Static Electricity
seo_title: Secondary 4 Physics: Static Electricity Worksheets (O-Level 6091 with Answers)
standard_text: State that there are positive and negative charges and that charge is measured in coulombs; state that unlike charges attract and like charges repel; explain electrostatic charging by friction in terms of the transfer of electrons; distinguish between electrical conductors and insulators; describe charging by induction and the role of earthing; describe an electric field as a region in which a charge experiences a force and draw field-line patterns for point charges and parallel plates; describe hazards and applications of static electricity (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Physics 6091 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Physics worksheets on static electricity: positive and negative charge, charging by friction and induction, earthing, electric fields, hazards and uses. 100 questions with answers.

body_html:
How to think about it

Objects become charged when electrons are transferred.

  • Rubbing moves electrons from one object to the other: the one that gains electrons becomes negative, the other positive by an equal amount.
  • Like charges repel; unlike charges attract; a charged object attracts a neutral one by induction.
  • Charging by induction: bring a charged rod near, earth the conductor, remove the earth, then remove the rod. The conductor gets the opposite charge.
  • Electric field lines point from + to −. Earthing and lightning conductors let charge flow safely to the ground.
Example

A polythene rod rubbed with wool becomes negative. What happened?

electrons moved from the wool to the rod

Answer: the wool becomes positive

Example

A positive rod is held near a sphere that is earthed, then earth removed, then rod removed. Charge?

electrons flow up from earth

they stay when earth is removed

Answer: negative

Common mistakes

  • Saying positive charges move when objects are rubbed. Only electrons move.
  • Thinking a neutral object has no charges. It has equal + and −.
  • Drawing field lines from − to +. They go from + to −.
  • Removing the rod before the earth connection in charging by induction.

faq.q: How does charging by friction work?
faq.a: Rubbing two insulators together transfers electrons from one to the other. The object that gains electrons becomes negative and the other becomes positive.
Charging a conductor without touching it: a nearby charged object moves its electrons, earthing lets electrons flow in or out, and the conductor is left with the opposite charge.

faq.q: Why is static electricity dangerous when refuelling?
faq.a: Friction can build up charge, and a spark could ignite fuel vapour, so vehicles and aircraft are earthed first.
